chapter.title: Memory: the intern forgets everything overnight

cards.body: Every morning the intern walks in with no memory of yesterday, none at all, so you hand them a folder: the task, every note so far, what happened at each step. They read it, do one thing, and the folder gets one page thicker. **The agent's memory is that folder, re-read from page 1 every single turn**, and by step 40 it is a brick.
cards.simpler: Picture a new intern who forgets everything each night. Every morning you hand them a folder: the task, every note so far, and what happened at each step. They read it all, do one thing, and add one page. **The agent's memory is that folder, read again from the first page every turn.** By step 40 the folder is as thick as a brick.

cards.prompt: The intern has done 12 steps on a task. Before step 13, what does the folder they are handed contain?

options.text: Just the goal and the last step. The rest is in their head.
The goal plus all 12 steps and their results, read again from the start.
Nothing. The intern remembers it all from yesterday.

whyNot.a: That's what a person would do, not a model: there is no 'in their head'. If it isn't in the folder, it doesn't exist.
whyNot.c: That's a human intern. The model is wiped after every single call, not just overnight.

cards.reteach: A model call is a one-off: text goes in, text comes out, and then it forgets everything. So the agent code pastes the whole history back in every turn. Step 13 sees the goal and steps 1 to 12, all over again.

cards.title: No memory, by design
cards.body:
A *model call* is one request: you send text, it sends text back. After that the model keeps nothing. Ask it the same question twice and it meets you fresh both times.

So how does an agent seem to remember? The agent code around the model keeps a *transcript*: the goal, every tool it asked for, every result that came back. Each turn, it sends the whole transcript to the model again.

**The agent remembers only what is written down and re-sent.** Nothing lives in the model between turns. That is the whole trick, and it is simpler than most people guess.
cards.simpler:
A model call is one request. You send text, it sends text back. After that the model keeps nothing. Ask it the same question twice and it starts fresh both times.

So how does an agent seem to remember? The code around the model keeps a transcript: the goal, every tool it asked for, every answer that came back. Each turn it sends the whole transcript again.

**The agent remembers only what is written down and sent again.** Nothing stays in the model between turns.

cards.title: Step 7 of the hotel search
cards.body: Maya asks an agent to find a hotel in Lisbon under 120 euros a night. By step 7 the transcript holds her request, 4 web searches, 2 page reads, and the prices they returned. Step 7 is the model reading all of that, top to bottom, and saying 'compare the two cheapest'. It does not remember doing steps 1 to 6. **It just reads about them**, the way you would read a stranger's notes, and then acts as if they were its own.
cards.simpler: Maya asks an agent to find a hotel in Lisbon for under 120 euros a night. By step 7 the transcript holds her request, 4 web searches, 2 page reads, and the prices they found. At step 7 the model reads all of that from top to bottom and says 'compare the two cheapest'. It does not remember doing steps 1 to 6. **It just reads about them**, like reading a stranger's notes, then carries on as if they were its own.

cards.prompt: An agent read a file at step 3. At step 9, the model needs a number from that file. Where can it get it?

options.text: From its own memory of doing step 3.
From the transcript, if the step 3 result is still in there.
It can't. Results from earlier steps are gone for good.

whyNot.a: That's a human's memory, not a model's. The model forgot step 3 the moment that call ended.
whyNot.c: That's the failure case, not the normal one. Earlier results stay available as long as they are still in the transcript being re-sent.

cards.reteach: Think of the folder. The file's contents were written into it at step 3. At step 9 the model reads the folder from page 1, so it sees that number again, unless someone trimmed the folder.

cards.title: The folder has a size limit
cards.body:
The model can only read so much text in one go. That limit is its *context window*: the most text one call can take in, prompt and transcript together. Think of it as how thick the folder may get.

A 10-step task fits easily. By step 40, with long tool results pasted in, the transcript nears the limit. The oldest pages get cut, the model loses the goal or a key result, and it repeats a step because it can no longer see that it already did it.

**Builders do 2 things about this.** They *summarise*: swap old steps for a short note of what was learned. And they keep *notes outside the transcript*: a file the agent writes to and reads back only when needed.
cards.simpler:
The model can only read so much text at once. That limit is called its context window. A 10-step task fits easily. By step 40 the transcript nears the limit. The oldest pages get cut, the model loses the goal, and it repeats a step it already did.

**Builders do 2 things about this.** They summarise old steps into a short note. And they keep notes in a file outside the transcript, read only when needed.

cards.body: Dev watches his agent sort 300 support tickets. Steps 1 to 25 are smooth. Around step 35 it starts re-opening tickets it already filed, politely, like a new person each time. He assumes the model got tired. It didn't: the transcript hit the window, the early steps dropped off, and the agent had no record it had done them. The tell is **repeating finished work with no sign it knows**.
cards.simpler: Dev watches his agent sort 300 support tickets. Steps 1 to 25 go smoothly. Around step 35 it starts re-opening tickets it already filed, politely, like a new person each time. He thinks the model got tired. It did not. The transcript hit the window, the early steps fell off, and the agent had no record it had done them. The clue is **repeating finished work with no sign it knows**.

cards.prompt: A friend says: 'My agent was great for 15 steps, then around step 45 it started asking the same question again. The model must be broken.' What's the better explanation?

options.text: The transcript outgrew the context window. Early steps got cut, so the model can't see it already asked.
The model got bored of the task and lost focus.
The tool it was using stopped working at step 45.

whyNot.b: That's a human intern's problem, not a model's. A model has no mood, only the text in front of it.
whyNot.c: That's a tool failure, which shows up as an error in the log, not as the agent redoing a step it already finished.

cards.reteach: The agent's whole memory is the transcript it re-sends each turn. When that transcript gets longer than the context window, the oldest parts are dropped. The agent then has no record it did step 12, so it does it again.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: **A model forgets everything the moment a call ends, so an agent fakes memory by re-sending the whole transcript every turn.** That transcript has a size limit, the context window, and when a long task hits it the agent starts losing the goal and repeating itself, which is why builders summarise old steps and keep notes in a file.
cards.simpler: **A model forgets everything the moment a call ends, so an agent fakes memory by sending the whole transcript again every turn.** That transcript has a size limit, called the context window. When a long task hits it, the agent starts losing the goal and repeating itself. That is why builders summarise old steps and keep notes in a file.

cards.body: Open any chatbot you use. Tell it your favourite colour. Start a **brand-new chat** and ask what it is. Most draw a blank. If yours remembers, it is using a notes file: thing 2 from this chapter.
cards.simpler: Open any chatbot you use. Tell it your favourite colour. Then start a **brand-new chat** and ask what your favourite colour is. Most will have no idea. If yours does remember, it is using a notes file, which is the second fix from this chapter.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now explain why an agent that worked for 10 steps can start repeating itself at step 40, and name the 2 things builders do about it.
